objective: Prove that in the quadrant (the box with both far walls removed) the corner contact (0, 1) returns, over GF(2), exactly at the times 4(2^j - 1): its return series is C(w^4), C(z) = sum_j z^(2^j - 1) the Catalan series mod 2, with first returns at 4 * 2^j. Secondary target, over the integers: the corner returns of length 4k number C_k^2, equivalently the simple walks in the quarter plane that never step west along the x-axis have C_k^2 excursions of length 2k.
status: Obstructed 2026-11-10 (pre-registered in a5769c7a7; refereed): A1 (the quadrant's corner series is C(w^4) mod 2) and A2 (C_k^2 returns of length 4k) not proved. Reduced by proof (Theorem 3, the column decomposition) to one identity on the half-line, [(I + sD + s^2 f(P))^-1]_00 = C(s^2). Proved also: the v-grid (Lemma 1), the reflection through the corner (Theorem 2), the plain quadrant even (Lemma 4), the looped half-line (Proposition 5), the kernel equation of the corner's column and the equivalence of A1 with a doubled identity. Computed: A1 below w^8000, A2 for k <= 24, the pairing of the corner's row and column.
title: The quadrant law
